Message

One row of an agent transcript: a prompt, the agent's text, a tool call, its result, a denial, usage or the end of a turn.

Status: draft

Examples

When to use it

  • For each event of an agent's turn, as a list item in the transcript's ol or ul, oldest first.
  • To show what a tool was asked to do and what it returned, in mono, at phone width.

When not to use it

  • For a request that still waits for the reader's answer. Use an approval, which carries Allow and Decline.
  • For the note that the agent is still working. Use streaming as the last row.
  • For a message about the app itself, such as a lost connection. Use an alert or a banner.

Variants

agent
The default, with no modifier class. Text the agent wrote. Label it with the agent's name.
user gw-message--user
A prompt the reader sent. Label it You.
tool-call gw-message--tool-call
A tool the agent ran: the tool name, then the command or path. Put long arguments in a details element whose summary keeps the label, the tool name and a short command.
tool-result gw-message--tool-result
What a tool returned. Show the first lines, and put the rest in a details element whose summary reads Show full output.
denied gw-message--denied
A call that was refused. Say what was not run and why.
usage gw-message--usage
A quiet line of figures for the turn, such as tokens and duration.
turn-end gw-message--turn-end
A quiet closing row under a rule, saying that the turn finished and how: completed, stopped or ended with an error.

Accessibility

  • Each row is an li in an ol or ul. Put role="log" and an accessible name on the list when rows are added while the reader watches, so new rows are announced.
  • Every row starts with gw-message__label, which says the kind in words: You, Claude Code, Tool call, Tool result, Denied, Usage, End. The kind is never the colour alone, and the denied row's icon is drawn by the stylesheet.
  • Write transcript text as text, never as markup, and write out characters that cannot be seen.
  • Collapsed arguments and long output use a native details element, with no script. Its summary holds text that says what is inside. Enter and Space open and close it, and its pointer target is 44px tall.
  • When output is cut short, the lines after the preview go in the details element, so opened text continues where the preview stopped.
  • The app sets nothing but the open attribute, which the browser manages.
